//: An example deployment schema, mounted with TelemetryEngine__SchemaFile.
The engine ships knowing none of these names. This file is what a deployment declares, and it
is a file rather than seventy indexed environment variables so it can be committed, diffed and
reviewed. An environment variable still overrides anything set here.
A dimension answers 'which one' and is a GROUP BY key. A measure answers 'how much' and is
aggregated, never grouped by. Removing a declaration is refused at boot while the column holds
The names below are a QR-menu deployment's vocabulary and mean nothing to the engine.

//Retention: Impressions are an order of magnitude more numerous than anything else here and are worth
nothing individually once daily_by_object has aggregated them.
A per-type entry can only ever be SHORTER than RetentionDays. ClickHouse evaluates every TTL
clause independently and any match deletes, so the shortest applicable rule wins no matter
what order they are written in — which means a longer entry would delete the rows on the base
schedule while claiming to keep them. The engine refuses to boot on that rather than let a
config file say one thing while the data says another.

Dimensions.//: Snapshotted onto the event, never joined at query time: when a photo is added in
Dimensions.//2: September, August must still compare as without-photo. A live join would report
Dimensions.//3: that every August impression had one.
Dimensions.Name: has_photo

Measures.//: Bounded because a forgotten tab is not a read. Out of range is rejected and counted,
Measures.//2: never clamped, so the loss is visible instead of silently changing the average.
Measures.Name: dwell_ms

Rollups.//: Answers the zero-impression and CTR reports without scanning raw. Impressions are
Rollups.//2: the highest-volume event by an order of magnitude, so this is the one that decides
Rollups.//3: whether the dashboard stays usable as venues are added.
Rollups.Name: daily_by_object

Rollups.//: One row per session rather than per time bucket, which is what replaces a scheduled
Rollups.//2: sessionizer. A job sweeping sessions idle for thirty minutes has to be re-run for
Rollups.//3: late arrivals and still leaves a hole when one lands after the re-run; a merge tree
Rollups.//4: fed by a view cannot, because a late event is just another partial state.
Rollups.//6: EventTypes is deliberately empty: a session rollup that filters them holds only
Rollups.//7: those rows, so its per-session event count is not the session's event count, and
Rollups.Name: sessions
